overall_mechanism_summary: Turgencin AMox1 and turgencin B have direct main-text biosensor evidence for rapid B. subtilis membrane-integrity/viability perturbation, but the evidence is species-limited and does not establish pore architecture or a molecular target. MIC/IC50 data remain phenotype-supported, methionine oxidation/envelope-affinity and NMR fold claims remain inferred, and TALOS+/MD/disulfide calculations remain computational/structural context only.
adjudicator_summary: Strongest supported mechanism is direct but bounded B. subtilis membrane-integrity/rapid-viability perturbation for turgencin AMox1 and turgencin B; E. coli short-window support is weak/negative, and molecular target/pore architecture remain untested.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper directly tested immediate membrane-integrity effects of turgencin AMox1 and turgencin B in B. subtilis pCSS962 luciferin biosensors; both affected B. subtilis membrane-integrity readouts, with turgencin B producing the faster and stronger luminescence decrease.

ontology_rules_applied.computational_only: Used for TALOS+, simulated annealing, disulfide-pattern energy comparisons, and MD structural support without experimental closure.
ontology_rules_applied.unknown_or_not_tested: Used for absent molecular target, depolarization, EM morphology, binding, enzyme, ribosome, or nucleic-acid mechanism assays.
